summary: Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot at Shofukuji (around 1949), president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies (1964).

Mun-keat Choong is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at the Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University, and the University of Queensland, completing an MA and PhD under the supervision of Roderick S. Bucknell.

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University. He served as assistant professor at Iwate University (around 1993–2004) and became a professor at Tohoku University around 2004.

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from Harvard. He was assistant professor at Tokyo Institute of Technology and Kyoto University before serving as professor at Kyoto (around 1990–2009).

Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1910 to 1913 and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki between roughly 1908 and 1961.

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall.

Muni Jinavijaya (1888–1976) was an Indologist and historian who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as principal of Gujarat Vidyapith around 1920 to 1929 and founded Rajasthan Puratana Granthamala (attested 1959).

Munish Chandra Joshi (1935–2007) worked in archaeology, history, and Indology. He served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (around 1989–1990) and Member Secretary at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (around 1995–2000).

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, Edgar H. Sturtevant, and Edward Sapir. He taught Latin at Yale and was professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Musashi Tachikawa (b. 1942) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya and Harvard universities under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held professorial posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam (b. 1947) is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, AMU, and JNU. He taught at JNU from around 1973 to 2001 and was appointed professor at the University of Chicago around 2001.

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at University College Dublin and in Europe. He taught at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, Wisconsin, and Chicago, and served as Director of the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (1960–1968).
Myokyo-ni (1921–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the University of Graz and trained under traditional teacher Sōkō Morinaga from around 1960 to 1972.
Myosei Tatsuguchi (b. 1934), also known as Akio Tatsuguchi, is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor (attested 1987) and later professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.
Myoshin Fujitake (b. 1956) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a committee member of the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000) and as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who studied at Madras Christian College. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore, and was professor at the University of Mysore.

Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She was a PhD student in Japanese studies at Eötvös Loránd University and studied under advisor Masanori Yamaji (attested 2016) as well as Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.
N. A. Gore was an Indology scholar who served as librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957–1958) and at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).

N. Aiyaswami Sastri was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Madras Sanskrit College and Visva-Bharati University. He held posts at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College, Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, and Visva-Bharati University.
N. D. Mironov (1880–1936) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Leipzig around 1902–1903 and under Heinrich Hübschmann as well as Hermann Jacobi.
